## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components can approach the streaming ceiling on low-churn workloads.

## Cache saturation
At death_q=0.01, ns/particle FALLS from 6.207 at N=10000 (past the L1d spill at N≈963, L2-resident) to 5.006 at N=100000 (past the L2 spill at N≈61680, DRAM-resident) to 4.51 at N=10000000 — no knee at either spill, only overhead amortization. At q=0.1 the curve is FLAT (6.383→5.945); at q=0.25 FLAT-to-rising (8.151→8.32); at q=0.5 FLAT at ~11.3 ns/p. Death rate raises the floor without changing the N-shape: churn flattens amortization because branchy respawn dominates per-particle cost regardless of cache residency.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 15.08 GB/s at N=10000000, q=0.01 — 50% of the 29.9 GB/s ceiling. At q=0.01 bandwidth rises with N (10.96→15.08 GB/s) as overhead amortizes but never exceeds half of ceiling. At q=0.1 it plateaus near 11 GB/s (37%), at q=0.25 near 8.2 GB/s (27%), at q=0.5 near 6.0 GB/s (20%). The algo is overhead-bound at small N and bandwidth-limited but sub-ceiling at large N/low churn, transitioning to branch-bound as death rate rises — branch_flush climbs from 8.1% (q=0.01, N=10M) to 42.4% (q=0.5, N=10M).

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized component-wise within one particle, not across particles. `ldr q1, [x25]` loads 4 floats from one particle; `ext.16b v3, v1, v2, #0xc` and `mov.s v3[3], v0[0]` pack them into a 4-lane vector; `fmul.4s` and `fadd.4s` update all 4 components at once. A gather appears: `ld1.s { v2 }[1], [x8]` loads one float into a single lane. The render loop uses `uqadd.8b` for byte saturating adds, but pixel writes are scalar `ldrb`/`strb` with `csel` clamping — scattered byte stores that cannot stream. Component-wise vec on the 68-byte stride explains the moderate bandwidth; byte-granular scatter caps it at 50% of ceiling.

## Verdict
Refuted — peak bandwidth is 15.08 GB/s, 50% of the 29.9 GB/s ceiling, even at q=0.01 and N=10M. Component-wise vectorization occurred (`fmul.4s`, `fadd.4s`), but the gather (`ld1.s`) and byte-granular scatter stores prevent streaming. At q≥0.25, branch_flush reaches 42–47%, collapsing bandwidth to 6–8 GB/s. Auto-vectorization over per-particle components does not approach the streaming ceiling in any regime.
